title: Karpenter — Extended Kubelet Config + CEL perf

options.content:
**Two `karpenter-*` pods, only one does work.** `charts/karpenter/values.yaml` sets `replicas: 2` with leader election, so every panel here is broken out `by (pod)` — expect one busy series and one near-flat standby. Do not sum them and call it "Karpenter's CPU".

**Rate windows are `[2m]`, not `[30s]`.** The scrape interval is 30s; a `[30s]` range holds one sample, and `rate()` needs two, so `[30s]` renders as gaps and dropouts. `[2m]` gives four samples per point.

**Idle Karpenter looks free.** With no reconcile churn these panels are flat regardless of what your change costs. Run `./churn.sh` while you watch, and read the *Instance-type re-resolutions* panel to confirm work is actually happening.

**The bottom row needs the ServiceMonitor** (`servicemonitor.yaml`). The top row comes from cAdvisor and works without it.

panels.title: Karpenter CPU usage (cores)
panels.description: cAdvisor, per pod. Container-level truth, includes GC and runtime overhead. No ServiceMonitor required.

panels.title: Karpenter memory — working set
panels.description: What the kernel would have to reclaim under pressure, and what the OOM killer compares against limits. Rises and does not come back down = leak candidate; take a heap profile.

panels.title: Instance-type re-resolutions (cache misses) — is work happening?
panels.description: The sanity-check panel. instancetype.(*Provider) caches resolved instance types under a key that hashes the kubelet block, so an unchanged EC2NodeClass never re-runs CEL. This is nodeclass reconcile throughput as a proxy: if it is flat, your profile will be empty and every other panel here is meaningless.

panels.title: nodeclass reconcile latency (p50 / p99)
panels.description: Where the CEL cost lands in wall-clock terms. Validation evaluates every expression against every instance type in the cache, so p99 here scales with (instance types x expressions). Compare perf-cel vs perf-static churn to separate CEL from the rest of the feature.

panels.title: Go allocation rate (bytes/sec)
panels.description: The most sensitive panel for this change. EvaluateExpression builds a fresh activation map per call, and it is called once per expression per instance type — ~800 x 6 per re-resolve. Allocation rate spikes on churn even when working-set memory looks flat, because the garbage is collected promptly. Confirm with ./profile.sh allocs.

panels.title: Go heap in use / goroutines
panels.description: Heap in use is the process-level counterpart to working set — it excludes the runtime's own overhead, so a gap between the two is not a leak. Goroutines should be flat; a ramp means something is being started per reconcile and never finishing.
